summary: Adds an OSS-native, isolated Plugin Manager for verified connected and offline installation planning, approved install and update execution, GitOps reconciliation, and Carbon administration workflows.
userImpact: Administrators can discover, review, install, update, retry, or cancel compatible plugin changes without building proprietary plugin source or maintaining customer-side CI.
Connected and air-gapped installations use the same digest-pinned signed release and lifecycle contracts.
Registry, entitlement, and deployment credentials remain outside the browser and ordinary EnterpriseGlue backend.

instructions: Deploy the optional Plugin Manager workload and configure its workload identity, trust policy, and deployment adapter before using managed plugin installation.
Keep the v0.14 eg-plugin CLI available for rollback and uninstall while those operations remain outside the v0.15 manager intent protocol.

configuration: Plugin Manager workload identity and internal control endpoint
Connected registry trust, private CA, and proxy settings
Compose planner or managed, Kubernetes, OpenShift, or offline deployment mode

changes: Adds versioned product discovery, installation intent, review, approval, observation, manager capability, release, and offline-delivery contracts.
Adds authorized browser-facing Plugin Manager administration endpoints and an internal pull-based manager protocol.

migrations: Adds plugin installation intent, approval, safe review, observation, and manager capability persistence.
notes: Plugin-owned data is isolated and is never deleted solely because entitlement expires.

security: All executable artifacts are addressed by immutable digest and verified against signed release, provenance, evidence, and revocation state before execution.
Approvals are bound to exact review and plan digests with expected revision and idempotency controls.
The manager is an internal-only isolated workload; ordinary backend and browser processes do not receive registry or deployment credentials.
documentation: Connected, offline, backup, recovery, and host-upgrade operations: `docs/runbooks/plugin-manager-operations.md`
knownLimitations: The enterpriseglue.ai commercial marketplace is deferred; v0.15 uses static/imported product descriptors and administrator-provided connected or offline delivery configuration.

The v0.15 manager protocol executes install and upgrade intents. Runtime enable/disable remains in the existing host controls, and rollback, export, and uninstall remain available through the retained v0.14 eg-plugin CLI until a later manager protocol version adds complete data-disposition and prior-release authority.
Whole-deployment host-upgrade preflight is not exposed by the v0.15 manager. Operators must run the existing compatibility-matrix verification before a host upgrade.
rollback: Disable the Plugin Manager workload to return to the v0.14 CLI/operator-managed lifecycle path.
Use retained exact prior plugin artifacts and the release rollback classification for plugin-specific rollback.
Database migrations include down paths and do not remove existing v0.14 plugin platform records.
validation: Contract schema and frozen compatibility fixtures
Manager restart, lease expiry, idempotent recovery, approval-digest, and revision-conflict tests
Connected OCI and signed offline install/update resolution, import, digest-plan binding, and fail-closed verification tests
Carbon component, authorization, paging, responsive, and deterministic screenshot coverage
Compose and Kubernetes/OpenShift adapter tests, clean-database migration, package boundary, image boundary, and release-policy gates
